items.review_rationale: Read both the quotient-topology statement and inverse-image criterion for the entire submersive map formulation. Surjectivity onto Y is indispensable, unlike strictness merely onto f(X); no open-map requirement is inferred.

references.context: Set theory and topology: surjective function f with image equal to all of Y

references.phrase: quotient topology on Y for f
references.context: Topology: final or quotient topology induced by a surjection X→Y
Set theory: inverse image or preimage of a subset under a function

references.disposition: The biconditional is the quotient-topology test; openness of f as a map is not asserted.

items.review_rationale: Read the definition relative to the specified ring homomorphism R→S. The closure consists of elements of S integral over the image of R; it is not the absolute integral closure of a field or the integral closure inside an unspecified fraction field.

references.context: Commutative algebra: subring of S containing the image of R with inherited ring operations

references.phrase: all elements integral over image of R
references.disposition: The quantified set comprehends integral elements inside S; the ambient ring S is part of the definition.

items.review_rationale: Read the full elementwise monic-polynomial criterion including the coefficient ring's image in S. No irreducibility or separability of the witnessing polynomial is implied.

references.phrase: monic polynomial over image of R
references.context: Commutative algebra: monic univariate polynomial with coefficients in the image of a ring map R→S
Ring theory: evaluation of polynomial at element s∈S yielding zero

references.disposition: This is existential and imposes neither minimality nor uniqueness of the polynomial.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the element-by-element universal quantification making a ring homomorphism integral: every s∈S is integral over R, with a possibly different monic polynomial for each s.

references.context: Commutative algebra: monic polynomial in R[T] whose value at s under R→S vanishes

references.disposition: The witness polynomial may depend on s; this does not require the ring homomorphism to be finite as a module.

items.review_rationale: Inspected the finite-generation-of-every-ideal characterization for a commutative unital ring. Distinguished ideal generation from finite cardinality of ideals and from requiring the ring itself to be finitely generated over another ring.

references.disposition: Finiteness is of a generating set of each ideal, not the number of elements in the ideal or the number of ideals.

items.review_rationale: Read this separate ACC formulation of Noetherianity: every ascending chain of ideals stabilizes. The chain is countably indexed but no descending-chain condition or Artinian hypothesis is being added.

references.context: Order theory: an increasing chain of subobjects eventually becomes constant

references.disposition: For each such sequence there is some index after which all successive ideals are identical; not a bound uniform across chains.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the maximal-condition characterization: each nonempty family of ideals contains a maximal member under set inclusion. Maximal here is within the chosen family, not a maximal proper ideal of R.

references.phrase: maximal element of a collection under inclusion
references.context: Order theory: maximal element of a specified partially ordered collection, not a global maximal ideal

references.disposition: The existence condition applies to each selected family and its internal inclusion order, not just to proper ideals.

items.review_rationale: Read the regular-module characterization with R acting on itself from the left. For commutative unital R, its submodules are exactly ideals; the Noetherian-module condition is not a module-freeness condition.

references.phrase: R acting on itself by multiplication
references.disposition: The standard regular module uses ring multiplication; it does not require an additional independently selected module action.
